title: Isochoric pressure at 0°C
description: Essential: Correctly calculates p0 using Charles's law for the isochoric process, yielding p0 = 273p1/(t1+273).

title: Isobaric volume at 0°C
description: Essential: Correctly calculates V2 using the ideal gas law, yielding V2 = 273p1V1/(p2(t1+273)).

title: Apply Charles's law
description: Important: For part (1), identifies the isochoric process and correctly applies p/T = constant, converting Celsius to Kelvin.

title: Apply ideal gas law
description: Important: For part (2), relates states using pV/T = constant, correctly incorporating given pressures p1 and p2 and volume V1.

title: Temperature conversion
description: Important: Consistently uses absolute temperature (Kelvin) in all gas law calculations, adding 273 to Celsius values.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Expresses final answers with appropriate units (Pa or N/m² for pressure, m³ for volume) or notes they are implied.

title: Misapplied process law
description: Pitfall: Uses Boyle's law (pV=constant) for the isochoric process or misidentifies which process uses which law.

title: Celsius-Kelvin error
description: Pitfall: Fails to convert Celsius to Kelvin in gas law ratios, e.g., using t1 directly instead of (t1+273).
